transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I just keep having these flashes. They hit me out of nowhere. It's like I'm suddenly right back in that crowded holding room, seeing that fight break out and hearing everyone getting shoved up against the wall. It happens even when I'm just standing at a pickup counter doing my route. I just can't seem to shake it.
How long ago did the incident in the holding room happen?
It was about a week ago. I got detained overnight, and... well, that's when I saw the assault happen in the holding area. So this has just been going on ever since then.
Since the incident, have you been avoiding anything that reminds you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. I've actually been turning down my night runs for work. And during the day, I... I take the long way around town on my routes just because I can't make myself go anywhere near that detention building. I've also been avoiding talking about what happened with anyone. If I try to talk about it, or if I even get close to that part of town, I just start feeling like I'm right back in that holding room.
Since the incident, have you felt unusually on guard or easily startled?

Yeah, definitely. It's... well, it's been pretty constant. Every radio crackle in my truck, a siren going off, or even just a slammed door makes me jump. It's like I'm bracing myself to get rushed. And after it happens, my heart just keeps pounding so hard that I actually have to pull over or step outside for a minute until it calms down.
Since the incident, have you had moments when you felt detached from yourself or as though the world around you was unreal?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really felt like that. Everything feels pretty real... maybe too real, honestly. I just feel constantly on edge, but I haven't felt disconnected from myself or anything like that.
Since the incident, have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, I barely sleep at all now. I'll maybe doze off for an hour or two, but then I'm just... I'm up. Usually because I'm having some dream about that cell, or I hear a door slam in my head. Once I'm awake, I can't get back to sleep. By the time morning rolls around, I just feel completely wrecked. It makes it really hard to focus on driving my route.
